title: Case #1: The Vanishing First Edition
summary: A priceless book disappears from a locked case. Only SELECT can say who took it.

steps.title: Case #1
body: Monday, 08:40. Odile Fenn, the owner of Inkwell & Ivy, is standing in front of an **empty display case**. Inside it, until last night, sat the shop's treasure: *The Ivy Ledger*, a 1931 first edition, item `11`. No sale was rung up. The case wasn't forced.
Rosa hands you the shop's event log. *"The case has an electronic lock, every staff badge scan is logged, and the till logs every sale. Somebody's story doesn't fit the data. Find them."*
Tables: `shop_log(id, at, person, action, item_id, note)` and `staff(name, role, shift_start, shift_end, has_key)`.
Each step uncovers one clue. Read each result before you move on.

steps.title: Clue 1: the book's day
prompt: Pull every log entry that touches item **11**, in time order. Return **at**, **person**, **action** and **note**.
Tables: `shop_log(id, at, person, action, item_id, note)` and `staff(name, role, shift_start, shift_end, has_key)`. Times are text like `'17:52'`, which sort and compare correctly as text.
setup: CREATE TABLE shop_log (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, at TEXT, person TEXT, action TEXT, item_id INTEGER, note TEXT);

INSERT INTO shop_log VALUES (1,'08:55','Juno Pike','open_shop',NULL,NULL),(2,'09:05','Wren Adair','display_check',11,'first edition in case'),(3,'10:12','Juno Pike','sale',3,NULL),(4,'11:30','Silas Crane','stock_in',7,'6 copies'),(5,'12:10',NULL,'door_chime',NULL,'front door'),(6,'13:45','Wren Adair','sale',1,NULL),(7,'15:00','Delivery','back_door',NULL,'courier drop-off'),(8,'16:20','Silas Crane','sale',4,NULL),(9,'17:15','Wren Adair','display_check',11,'first edition in case'),(10,'17:30','Wren Adair','clock_out',NULL,NULL),(11,'17:48','Juno Pike','sale',6,NULL),(12,'17:50','Silas Crane','stockroom',NULL,'sorting returns'),(13,'17:52',NULL,'case_open',11,'display case unlocked'),(14,'17:54','Juno Pike','sale',10,NULL),(15,'17:56',NULL,'case_close',11,NULL),(16,'17:58','Silas Crane','back_door',NULL,'carrying a parcel'),(17,'18:02','Juno Pike','close_shop',NULL,NULL);
CREATE TABLE staff (name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, role TEXT, shift_start TEXT, shift_end TEXT, has_key INTEGER);

INSERT INTO staff VALUES ('Juno Pike','manager','08:30','18:30',1),('Wren Adair','bookseller','09:00','17:30',1),('Silas Crane','stock clerk','11:00','19:00',1),('Pip Morrow','weekend help','10:00','16:00',0),('Odile Fenn','owner','12:00','17:00',1);
steps.explain: The book was in its case at 17:15. At 17:52 the case was opened, and nobody's name is on the entry.

prompt: Somebody opened the case without scanning a badge. List every log entry with **no person recorded**, in time order: **at**, **action**, **note**.

steps.explain: Three unbadged events. The door chime at noon is a customer. The case was opened at 17:52 and closed at 17:56: a four-minute job.

steps.title: Clue 3: who could open it?
prompt: The case needs a key. Find the staff who **have a key** (`has_key = 1`) and were **on shift at 17:52** (their shift started at or before 17:52 and ended at or after it).

steps.title: Clue 4: alibis
prompt: What were the two suspects doing around the moment the case was opened? Return **at**, **person**, **action** and **note** for every entry by **Juno Pike** or **Silas Crane** between **17:45 and 18:00** (inclusive), in time order.

steps.title: Name the culprit
prompt: One last piece. The culprit left the building with the book. Return the **person** (just that one column, once) who went out the **back door** **after 17:52**.
